headline: Past {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, a point of pass rate costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month, not {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}; the owner picks where to stop.
lede: A single retry raises pass rate at every model and reasoning level for little cost and a longer p95 tail, and every Atlas-M setting but the most expensive is matched or beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S one. A pass-rate floor above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} or a p95 budget under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} would move the lean.
flag: No pass-rate floor, latency budget or value per point was declared before the run, and no configuration served as a control. The lean below is the analyst's, not a rule.

caveats.material_if: if the declared volume counts tasks rather than planner calls: each option's monthly cost then scales by its own calls per task ({measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for the lean, {measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} for {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}). Every dollar band on this page moves with the basis, so a declared value per point can land in a different band. Only the order of the options holds either way.
only if the owner would pay for the steps above the lean: each adds under a point of pass rate and nothing shows it is more than noise. The steps up to the lean are larger.
only if the lean's edge over its neighbours is the reason to choose it: picked as the knee of {n_candidates|int} configurations, its estimate is the optimistic one.
only if the check fails plans the product would accept, as on ambiguous names, where a clarifying question is the only pass.

decision.text: Moving from the lean to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} adds {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap} a month to the lean's {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} for {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points of pass rate, and lengthens the p95 tail. Each step up to the lean cost at most {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a point. Every dollar figure is priced per planner call.

The lean is the cheapest option for any pass-rate floor above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}. Above that the cheapest is {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, and above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} qualifies. A p95 budget under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} rules the lean out.

Ours, not a declared rule: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}. Priced per call, it is the best option for any value of a point between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month.

Declarations from the planner's owner: first whether the monthly volume counts tasks or calls, which fixes the dollar bands; then a pass-rate floor and a p95 budget, or a monthly value for a point of pass rate, which picks the band.

Multi-hop is the lean's weakest task, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}. The step to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} lifts it to {task.multihop.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.mean}, more than the {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points the step adds overall, so an owner who weights multi-hop gets more for the step than its overall price says.

claims.text: Pass rate climbs steeply with cost up to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and flattens after it: the next point costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month, against {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} for the last one before it.

evidence.caption: Every configuration's pass rate against its cost per call, cost on a log axis. The upper-left edge is the frontier: from Nano-XS through {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}.
The frontier options, cheapest first: the figures each price step is computed from.

claims.text: A single retry raises pass rate at every model and reasoning level, most where the base is weakest: on Nano-XS with reasoning off it adds {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points for {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap} a month.

evidence.caption: Model by reasoning level and retry. Each tile holds pass rate, cost per call and p95 latency; each retry column sits right of its no-retry pair. The pills read not gated because no gate was declared.

claims.text: Atlas-M reaches the frontier only at its top setting: each of its other settings is matched or beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S one, and the top one adds {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.gain|abs|pts} points over {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} for {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap} more a month.

evidence.caption: Each Atlas-M setting after the cheaper Brisk-S setting that matches or beats it, ending with {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, which none does. {arm:atlas-m.low.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} tie on pass rate.

claims.text: The dearer options are slower in the tail: {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} has a p95 of {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95}, against {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} for {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95 for the shortlist. No budget was declared, so no line is drawn.

claims.text: Multi-hop is the weakest task for every option on the shortlist; {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} passes {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} of it.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the shortlist. Descriptive: no interval, and task sizes are not stated.

claims.text: Each failure card the snapshot froze for the lean shows a planning slip a fix could target: a second hop folded into the first, a date window off by a day, an ambiguous name answered without asking. The cards are a sample, not a census; the date-window card names its slip the commonest wrong-argument pattern.

evidence.caption: The failure cards the snapshot froze for {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}: multi-hop, date math and ambiguous names, with none for single lookup. The snapshot chose them, not the size of each task's loss.

explore.binds: Which configurations qualify, and so the cheapest one that does.
explore.outcome: Up to {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean} a Nano-XS setting is cheapest, and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} it is {arm:brisk-s.low.r0}. Above that and up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} the lean is. Above that {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is, and above {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} qualifies.

Under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} the lean is out. Under {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} every Atlas-M setting is out as well. No budget above {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95} binds anything.

explore.control: Monthly value of a point of pass rate
explore.binds: Which frontier option is best, priced per planner call.
explore.outcome: The lean is best between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}. {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is best up to {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, and {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} above it. On a per-task basis every band moves (see the cost-basis caveat).

omitted.what: Code's dominance call naming Nano-XS with reasoning off and no retry dominant
omitted.why: It ranks on cost alone because no quality axis was declared, and that configuration has the lowest pass rate; Method says why the report reads the pass-rate frontier instead.

omitted.why: It appears only in the cost-basis caveat: it changes no option's place on the frontier, but it moves the dollar bands if the volume counts tasks.
The snapshot lists them but holds no figures for any configuration.

omitted.what: Brisk-S at low reasoning with no retry
omitted.why: It sits on the cost and pass-rate edge but is best at no value of a point; it matters only under a p95 budget between its tail and the lean's, which the explore control covers.

omitted.what: Task-level pass rates for the configurations off the shortlist
omitted.why: Multi-hop is weakest in each of them too; the appendix holds them, and they change no call.
It belongs to a configuration off the shortlist; retry recovering truncated output is already shown by the retry claim.

next.text: State whether the declared monthly volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int} counts tasks or planner calls.
next.settles: Which dollar bands apply. Every price per point here is per call; on a task basis each option's cost scales by its own calls per task, so the bands move and a declared value per point can fall in a different band.

next.text: The planner's owner declares a pass-rate floor and a p95 latency budget, or a monthly value for a point of pass rate.
next.settles: Which band applies, which turns the trade into a decision.

next.text: The owner defines what makes a planned call pass, including whether a clarifying question is the only pass on ambiguous names.
next.settles: Whether the ambiguous-name rates, and so every option's overall rate, measure the product's own bar.

next.text: Rerun {arm:nano-xs.high.r1}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} paired on the same cases, with an interval on each difference.
next.settles: Whether the steps either side of the lean are real or noise; the gain above it is under a point and carries no interval.

next.text: Target the lean's slips, with a bounds check on date windows and a prompt that plans each hop separately, then rerun it.
next.settles: Whether the lean closes part of its gap to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} at its own price, which would make the dearer steps harder to justify.

method.text: Each configuration ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases|int} cases, none lost or failed. Repeats and task sizes are not stated.
{arm:nano-xs.high.r1}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} and {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}: the frontier options a decider would weigh, from the best Nano-XS setting up.

The campaign does not define what makes a planned call pass. The failure cards count missing calls, wrong arguments, wrong tools and malformed output as failures, and on ambiguous names only a clarifying question passes.
None. Every pass rate is a point estimate with no interval or correction, so no difference between configurations is tested.
Rates print to the nearest tenth, without a trailing zero, and gains are computed before rounding, so a quoted gain can differ by a tenth of a point from the difference of the printed rates.
Arithmetic on point estimates: the extra monthly cost of the next frontier option divided by the points it adds. It describes; it does not infer.
Cost is per planner call, which the lattice tiles label a reply. Monthly cost is that figure at the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int} a month.
p50 and p95 per configuration. Retry leaves p50 unchanged and lengthens p95.

Code's dominance computation names {arm:nano-xs.off.r0} dominant because, with no criteria declared, cost is its only axis. That configuration has the lowest pass rate, {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0.mean}, so the report reads the frontier on pass rate and cost instead.
No production configuration served as a control. Only model, reasoning level and retry were varied.
